War Bird
CR 1

The bronze feathers of these terrifying birds gleam in the sun as they circle above their prey.

XP 400
CE Medium magical beast
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 12, touch 11, flat-footed 11 (+1 Dex, +1 natural)
hp +15 (2d10+4)
Fort +5, Ref +4, Will +1
DR 5/bludgeoning; Resist fire 5
Weaknesses vulnerable to sonic

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., fly 40 ft. (good)
Melee 2 talons +4 (1d6+2)
Ranged feather dart +3 (1d4+2) range 20 ft., crit 20×2

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 9, Wis 12, Cha 12
Base Atk +2; CMB +4; CMD 15
Feats Flyby Attack
Skills Fly +5, Perception +7; Racial Modifiers +2 Perception
Languages –

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Feather Regrowth (Ex)

The war bird has twenty-four feathers it can hurl. Used feathers replenish every morning at dawn.

Dive (Ex)

If the war bird is flying and dives at least 15 feet straight toward a target and then hits the target with a talon attack on the same turn, the attack deals an extra (2d6) slashing damage.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts, hills, mountains, plains (Abyss)
Organization solitary, pair, or gaggle (3-12)
Treasure none

Originating from a lower plane, war birds are magical beings whose connection to Ares is as old as the gods themselves.

These magnificent creatures once flew too close to Hephaestus’ forge. The intense heat and raw power of the forge infused their bodies, transforming their feathers into bronze.

The war bird’s breast is covered in bronze feathers. This plumage protects the creature from harm and can be used as darts which the bird hurls down on enemies.

War birds take their role as temple guardians with the utmost dedication. They are fierce defenders, patrolling the skies with unwavering vigilance. The sight of these majestic creatures soaring above serves as a warning to would-be intruders. With keen eyes and acute perception, they detect even the slightest signs of danger, ready to unleash their aerial onslaught upon those who would disturb the hallowed ground.

Binding

To bind war birds to a temple of Ares, a priestess of Ares performs sacred rituals involving offerings of blood, sacred incantations, and the communion of divine energy. Through these ceremonies, the war birds become attuned to the temple’s sacred grounds.
